title: VideoGameQA-Bench: Evaluating Vision-Language Models for Video Game Quality Assurance
key_findings: Standard zero-shot VLMs detect coarse bugs (~78% accuracy) but fail severely on micro-clipping and precise bounding boxes, frequently hallucinating on stylized art.
primary_limitations: High inference latency (>1.5s/frame); poor spatial bounding localization for subtle geometry defects.

title: A Hybrid Co-Finetuning Approach for Visual Bug Detection in Video Games
key_findings: Co-finetuning leveraging labelled target frames, co-domain games, and unlabelled gameplay frames boosts recall by +18.4% mAP without manual exhaustive labels.
primary_limitations: Significant cross-domain degradation when transferring across radically divergent art styles (e.g. realistic 3D to voxel).

title: State-Aware Visual Glitch Detection in Complex 3D Video Games Using Deep Multimodal Representations
key_findings: Fusing game-engine internal telemetry (transform matrices and collision queries) with RGB vision reduces false positives by 42% compared to pure vision.
primary_limitations: Requires engine-level instrumentation hooks; cannot be deployed as a black-box tester on closed commercial builds.

title: How Far Can VLMs Go for Visual Bug Detection? Studying 19738 Keyframes from 41 Hours of Gameplay Videos
key_findings: Baseline VLM achieves 0.50 precision and 0.72 accuracy; secondary judge models and report-retrieval prompting provide only marginal gains while inflating compute cost.
primary_limitations: Low temporal sensitivity; prompt sensitivity; prone to mistaking intentional stylized art for visual defects.

title: RefGlitch-Bench: A Benchmark for Reference-based Gameplay Glitch Detection with Vision-Language Models
authors: Yu, Wiens, Barahona-Rios, Wilkins, Zadtootaghaj, Barman, Bezemer
key_findings: Formulating glitch detection as an explicit within-video comparison with a reference frame (Last Clean Frame) dramatically reduces false alarms and resolves ambiguity.
primary_limitations: Requires reliable reference frame selection; error propagation occurs when the selected reference frame itself contains subtle artifacts.

title: TempGlitch: Detecting Temporal Visual Glitches in Continuous Gameplay Video Streams
key_findings: Single-frame anomaly detectors miss over 65% of animation and flickering glitches; sliding-window temporal attention over 16-frame buffers is essential for streaming playtests.
primary_limitations: High computational footprint; current video transformer backbones are too heavy for 60 FPS real-time CI playtesting.

title: Weak Supervision for Label Efficient Visual Bug Detection in Video Games
key_findings: Domain-specific weak supervision with just 5 clean exemplar frames improves F1 score from 0.336 to 0.550 in low-prevalence first-person player clipping regimes.
primary_limitations: Evaluated primarily on first-person clipping in a single open-world game; generalisation to other glitch classes unverified.

title: Automatically Detecting Visual Bugs in HTML5 Canvas Games
key_findings: Internal canvas decomposition and oracle sprite comparison achieves 100% accuracy on injected canvas bugs vs 44.6% for naive screenshot diffing.
primary_limitations: Restricted to 2D web canvas games with static sprites; inapplicable to dynamic 3D lighting and complex vertex shaders.

title: Video Game Automated Testing Approaches: An Assessment Framework
key_findings: Comprehensive framework categorizing game testing techniques; establishes visual regression as the least automated and most vulnerable testing sector.
primary_limitations: Taxonomic review without deep learning implementation or empirical CV benchmark.

title: A Literature Review of Software Testing Practices and Frameworks in the Video Gaming Industry
key_findings: Reveals that while game logic unit tests are automating rapidly, visual QA remains over 80% manual in industry due to brittle computer vision tooling.
primary_limitations: General software engineering scope; lacks technical algorithmic analysis of modern CV/VLM architectures.

title: A Large-Scale Empirical Study of Video Game Testing Practices
key_findings: Empirical mining of 1M+ player reviews proves graphical bugs and mesh collision clipping are the primary drivers of negative launch sentiment and refund requests.
primary_limitations: Focuses on defect perception and triage rather than algorithmic computer vision detection.

title: Video game testing: a systematic literature review
key_findings: Foundational baseline demonstrating historical lack of computer vision in game testing; early work was confined to headless asserts and fragile pixel diffing.
primary_limitations: Historical review preceding the modern deep learning and VLM revolution.

title: Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning for Object Clipping Detection in Modern 3D Engines
key_findings: Self-supervised contrastive learning detects subtle mesh clipping (AUROC 89.6%) without requiring exhaustive human manual glitch annotations.
primary_limitations: Evaluated in controlled Unreal Engine testbeds; organic in-game ragdoll collisions exhibit higher variance.

title: Automating Playtesting for Glitch Detection in 3D Games
model_family: PPO RL Agent + VAE Anomaly Detection
key_findings: Reinforcement learning agents navigating 3D levels discover collision nulls and world void holes leading to out-of-bounds player drops.
primary_limitations: Heavily overfits to specific geometry layouts; lacks zero-shot cross-level and cross-game transferability.

title: Deep visual anomaly detection for 3D game environments using multi-view surface projections
key_findings: Surface projection patch memory banks detect broken polygonal meshes and vertex stretching without damaged mesh training samples.
primary_limitations: Degrades under dynamic real-time day/night lighting cycles and atmospheric particle effects.

title: Grammar-Based and Constraint-Driven Testing for Collision and Clipping Anomalies in 3D Environments
key_findings: Constraint verification combined with camera-space boundary matching identifies non-physical penetrations where colliders detach.
primary_limitations: Limited to simple indoor environments with convex polygonal bounding boxes.

title: Real-Time Shading and Texture Pop-in Glitch Localization in Continuous 3D Streams
key_findings: Differentiates intentional player camera sweeps from mipmap stalling, LOD pop-in, and coplanar Z-fighting at 75 FPS real-time.
primary_limitations: High GPU VRAM overhead; susceptible to motion blur artifacts during extreme angular velocity whip pans.

title: Effective Visual Regression Testing for Web and Interactive Applications with Perceptual Image Differencing
key_findings: Human Contrast Sensitivity Function filters out sub-pixel antialiasing noise and floating-point shader discrepancies across GPUs.
primary_limitations: Inapplicable to non-deterministic 3D environments with dynamic particle simulations.

title: ShaderBug: Automated Shader Defect and Rendering Regression Detection via Mutational Fuzzing
key_findings: Automated shader mutation detects catastrophic rendering crashes, NaN/Inf pixel explosions, and inverted surface normal bugs.
primary_limitations: Focusses on compiler/driver rendering faults rather than asset composition and artistic integration.

title: Action-Conditioned Gameplay Video Anomaly Detection
key_findings: Conditioning video anomaly prediction on player controller inputs eliminates false positives caused by sudden intentional player motions.
primary_limitations: Requires synchronized game controller telemetry logs alongside video streams.

title: GlitchHunter: Automated Detection of Character Rigging and Animation Defects in 3D Games
key_findings: Keypoint tracking with Spatio-Temporal GCNs identifies joint hyper-extensions, bone collapsing, and missing blending transitions (92.4% acc).
primary_limitations: Requires exposed skeletal bone coordinate data or accurate 2D pose estimation from screen pixels.

title: Wuji: Automatic Online Combat Game Testing via Deep Reinforcement Learning and Evolutionary Algorithms
authors: Zheng, Xie, Shen, Chen, Ji, Liu
key_findings: Evolutionary RL agents autonomously discover level boundary tears, collision nulls, and out-of-bounds camera voids in production games.
primary_limitations: Requires substantial cloud training compute; agents do not understand high-level semantic game objectives.

title: Autonomous VLM Agents for Exploratory Playtesting and Interactive Bug Localization
key_findings: Multimodal agents playtest 3D games via gamepad inputs, identify visual anomalies, and file natural language bug reports with screenshots.
primary_limitations: High API token cost; agents occasionally loop in navigation dead ends.

title: VLM-UI-Test: Autonomous GUI Testing of Video Games Using Multimodal Foundation Models
key_findings: Verifies that HUD elements, mini-maps, and health bars never occlude interactable world targets or suffer aspect ratio text clipping.
primary_limitations: Requires high-resolution frame sampling to detect fine-grained text overflow in mini-maps.

title: GlitchBench: Can Large Multimodal Models Detect Video Game Glitches?
key_findings: Early multimodal models achieved only 57.2% overall accuracy, frequently failing on localized polygon stretching and subtle texture seams.
primary_limitations: Evaluated only static single frames; early generation VLMs lacked temporal reasoning and Chain-of-Thought prompting.

title: VideoGameBunny: Towards Vision Assistants for Video Games
key_findings: Instruction fine-tuning on gaming visual instruction pairs improves game jargon understanding and bug localization by +14.6% over vanilla base models.
primary_limitations: High fine-tuning computational overhead; relies on generated QA pairs that may reflect teacher model hallucinations.

title: PhysGame: Uncovering Physical Commonsense Violations in Gameplay Videos
authors: Cao, Tang, Zhao, Guo, Liu, Zhang, Liu, Sun, Reid, Liang
key_findings: Curated 880 real game glitch clips across kinematics and mechanics; shows current video models fail to detect 62% of unnatural momentum and gravity violations.
primary_limitations: Only contains glitch clips without paired clean baseline videos from the same game session.

title: CLIP Meets GamePhysics: Towards Bug Identification in Gameplay Videos Using Zero-Shot Transfer Learning
key_findings: First study showing CLIP text-to-image matching can identify buggy video moments via text queries (e.g. flying car, spinning ragdoll) without training.
primary_limitations: Suffers high false positive rates when game background semantics overpower bug keywords.

title: Large Language Models Are Pretty Good Zero-Shot Video Game Bug Detectors
key_findings: Zero-shot prompt-based LLMs classify game bug reports and textual logs with 78% accuracy prior to multimodal adoption.
primary_limitations: Text-only; cannot inspect actual pixel rendering or spatial mesh collisions.

title: LeCuration: A Tiny World Model as a Data Curation Mechanism for Game QA
model_family: Latent World Models (Recurrent State Space Models)
key_findings: World models predicting latent future game frames flag sudden rendering discontinuities and pop-ins as high-entropy surprise events.
primary_limitations: Requires predictable camera trajectories; high player agency and rapid scene switching triggers false surprise spikes.

title: Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks to Detect Rendered Glitches in Video Games
key_findings: Seminal industrial paper showing CNNs can detect missing textures and stretched meshes at 85% accuracy on synthetic training corruptions.
primary_limitations: Trained strictly within a single game engine; zero cross-title generalisation.

title: Automated Visual Bug Detection in 3D Video Games Using Deep Convolutional Networks
key_findings: Demonstrates that convolutional detectors degrade severely when tested on unseen 3D asset geometries and non-standard camera angles.
primary_limitations: Small dataset (<2,000 images); limited bug taxonomy.

title: Learning to Identify Perceptual Bugs in 3D Video Games
key_findings: Unsupervised reconstruction loss flags texture swimming and shader degradation without defect-specific manual labels.
primary_limitations: Cannot distinguish artistic shader stylization from genuine rendering defects.

title: Automated Glitch Detection in Games Using Supervised Neural Classifiers
key_findings: Examines classifier sensitivity to dynamic illumination; shows lighting shifts cause up to 28% drop in CNN bug classification accuracy.
primary_limitations: Relies on synthetic procedural glitch injection rather than natural organic game defects.

title: Inspector: Pixel-Based Automated Game Testing via Exploration, Detection, and Investigation
authors: Liu, Cai, Zhao, Qin, Brown, Bischoff, Liu
model_family: Curiosity RL Exploration + Vision Anomaly Head
key_findings: End-to-end framework combining reinforcement learning exploration with pixel-based anomaly detection on commercial Xbox builds.
primary_limitations: Black-box exploration struggles to navigate complex quest progression gates.

title: RiverGame: A Game Testing Tool Using Artificial Intelligence
key_findings: Comprehensive automated testing framework coupling state-transition models with deep visual assertion oracles.
primary_limitations: Requires game state formalization; heavy manual setup overhead per game.

title: GELID: Game Glitch Identification from Video Captions
key_findings: Extracts bug timestamps from long gameplay videos by analyzing streamer audio transcripts and automated speech recognition without processing raw video frames.
primary_limitations: Only works on gameplay footage with expressive human commentary; inapplicable to silent automated CI soak runs.

title: HASTE: Image-Similarity Based Stuttering Bug Event Detection in Gameplay Videos
model_family: Temporal Perceptual Hashing & Optical Flow Differencing
key_findings: Detects micro-stutters and frame pacing hitches from video streams by analyzing inter-frame optical flow dissimilarity curves.
primary_limitations: Focuses exclusively on temporal frame rate stability; cannot detect static spatial or texture corruptions.

title: Classifying Gameplay Video Segments as Buggy or Non-Buggy Using Captions
key_findings: Shows that player verbal expressions (exclamations, confusion) paired with video features achieve 83.4% bug detection accuracy.
primary_limitations: Dependent on vocal streamer presence; cannot be deployed on headless continuous integration test runs.

title: GLIB: Towards Automated Test Oracle for Graphically-Rich Applications
authors: Chen, Li, Chen, Fan, Hu, Yang
key_findings: Automated layout verification discovering 127 visual UI bugs in production graphical applications using visual element hierarchy graphs.
primary_limitations: Designed for 2D UI layouts; inapplicable to dynamic 3D world viewports.

title: Q-Bench: A Benchmark for General-Purpose Foundation Models on Low-Level Vision
authors: Wu, Zhang, Zhang, Chen, Liao, Wang, Li, Sun, Yan, Zhai, Lin
key_findings: Comprehensive proof that high-level semantic VLMs perform poorly at low-level pixel perception (blur, noise, fine-grained rendering artifacts).
primary_limitations: General computer vision benchmark; not specialized to interactive video game engines.

title: A Survey of Video Game Testing
key_findings: Documents that visual regression testing is the least automated sector (<15% automation) across the entire game development lifecycle.
primary_limitations: Taxonomic survey; no empirical CV benchmark.

title: Know Your Bugs: A Survey of Issues in Automated Game Testing Literature
key_findings: Synthesizes academic bug classifications with industrial JIRA schemas, demonstrating severe fragmentation in visual bug definitions.
primary_limitations: Survey without technical CV implementation.

title: Automated Reporting and Verification of Visual GUI Defects in Interactive Applications
key_findings: Automated CV framework verifying visual defect reproduction from screenshots and user reports, achieving 94% precision in GUI element detection.
primary_limitations: Focused on mobile/desktop GUI widgets; not tailored to real-time 3D camera viewports.

title: Towards Automated UI Visual Bug Detection in Cross-Platform Mobile and PC Games
model_family: Deep Object Detection & Aspect Ratio Bounds
key_findings: Identifies that non-standard aspect ratios (ultrawide 21:9, mobile notches) cause 34% of player-reported interface text and HUD clipping bugs.
primary_limitations: Small evaluation scale; evaluated only static screens.
